reason: The text explicitly portrays Yahweh as protective and liberating toward the Hebrew people (Israel), not antagonistic. God directs the plagues against Egypt and Pharaoh, while actively shielding Israel: the land of Goshen is spared from the flies plague ('I will separate my people from your people'), and during the darkness plague, 'all the children of Israel had light in their dwellings' (וּֽלְכָל־ בְּנֵ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל הָ֥יָה א֖וֹר בְּמוֹשְׁבֹתָֽם). God's purpose is explicitly to free Israel from bondage ('Let my people go that they may serve me'). The antagonism is directed toward Pharaoh and Egypt, not toward the Hebrew people.
